===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=land|:inh|enm:schore<ety:inh<ang:*sċora>>}}
From {{inh|en|enm|schore}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*sċora}} (attested as ''sċor-'' in placenames), from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skurô|t=rugged rock, cliff, high rocky shore}}. Possibly related to {{cog|ang|sċieran||to cut}}, which survives today as {{cog|en|shear|}}.

Cognate with {{cog|dum|scorre||land washed by the sea}}, {{cog|gml|schor||shore, coast, headland}}, {{cog|gmh|schorre}} {{gloss|"rocky crag, high rocky shore"; > {{cog|de|Schorre}},  {{m|de|Schorren|t=towering rock, crag}}}}, and {{cog|li|sjaor||riverbank}}. Maybe connected with {{cog|nb|skjær}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
#: {{ux|en|lake '''shore''';  bay '''shore''';  gulf '''shore''';  island '''shore''';  mainland '''shore''';  river '''shore''';  estuary '''shore''';  pond '''shore''';  sandy '''shore''';  rocky '''shore'''}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Complaints|Visions of the Worlds Vanitie
|passage=the fruitful '''shore''' of muddy Nile}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=Now we plunged into a deep shade with the boughs lacing each other overhead, and crossed dainty, rustic bridges{{...}}: or anon we shot into a clearing, with a colored glimpse of the lake and its curving '''shore''' far below us.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1958
|author=Wang Chun-heng
|chapter=The Middle Yangtse Region
|title=A Simple Geography of China
|url=https://archive.org/details/dli.pahar.3127/
|series=China Knowledge Series
|location=Peking
|publisher=w:Foreign Languages Press
|OCLC=185443676
|page=117
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/dli.pahar.3127/page/117/
|text=Floods in the middle Yangtse were frequent in the past. The Yangtse carries less silt than the Yellow River. But under the old regimes, the Chingkiang section (the section of the middle Yangtse between Chihchiang County in Hupeh Province and Chenglingchi in Hunan Province), the '''shores''' of the Tungting Lake and the lower reaches of the Han Shui were frequently flooded, causing great damage to the vast plain of Hupeh and Hunan.}}
# {{lb|en|from the perspective of one on a body of water}} Land, usually near a port.
#: {{ux|en|The [[seamen]] were serving on '''shore''' instead of on ships.}}
#: {{ux|en|The passengers signed up for '''shore''' tours.}}

=====Usage notes=====
* Generally, only the largest of rivers, which are often estuaries, are said to have '''''shores'''''.
* Rivers and other flowing bodies of water are said to have {{m|en|bank|banks}}.
* ''River bank(s)'' outnumbers ''River shore(s)'' about 200:3 at [[COCA]].

# {{lb|en|obsolete|intransitive}} To arrive at the shore

===Etymology 2===
From Late {{inh|en|enm|shore|t=a prop, a support}}{{nb...|schore, score|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=shōre|pos=''n.''(3)|noformat=1|id=MED40043}}</ref> from {{der|en|dum|schore}}, {{m|dum|schare|t=a prop, a stay}} (modern {{cog|nl|schoor}}), and {{der|en|gml|schōre}}, {{m|gml|schāre|t=a prop, a stay; barrier; stockade}} (compare {{cog|non|skorða|t=a prop, a stay}} ({{cog|no|skor}}, {{m|no|skorda}})); further etymology unknown.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''n.''{{sup|3}}|noformat=1|id=178551|date=March 2021|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|alt=shore{{sup|2}}|pos=n}}</ref>

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A [[prop#Noun|prop]] or [[strut#Noun|strut]] [[support#Verb|supporting]] some [[structure#Noun|structure]] or [[weight#Noun|weight]] above it.
#: {{ux|en|The '''shores''' stayed upright during the earthquake.}}

===Etymology 3===
[[File:Shore (PSF).png|thumb|A [[boat#Noun|boat]] on [[dry land]] which has been shored up ''(etymology 3)'' to keep it [[upright#Adjective|upright]].]]

From Late {{inh|en|enm|shoren|t=to prop, to support}}{{nb...|schore, ssore|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=shōren|pos=''v.''(1)|noformat=1|id=MED40045}}</ref><ref>Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=''v.''{{sup|1}}|noformat=1|id=178556|date=March 2021|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|alt=shore{{sup|2}}|pos=v}}</ref> from {{inh|en|enm|shore|t=a prop, a support}} (see [[#Etymology 2|etymology 2]]) + {{m|enm|-en|pos={{glossary|suffix}} forming the {{glossary|infinitive}} form of {{glossary|verb}}s}};<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=-en|pos=''suf.''(3)|noformat=1|id=MED13518}}</ref> compare {{cog|dum|schooren|t=to prop up, support}} and {{cog|gml|schore|t=to shovel; to sweep}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}} {{tlb|en|transitive}}

# ''Not followed by'' '''[[up]]''': to [[provide]] (something) with [[support#Noun|support]].
#: {{synonyms|en|buttress|reinforce|strengthen|support}}
# ''Usually followed by'' '''up''': to [[reinforce]] (something [[at risk]] of [[failure]]).
#: {{synonyms|en|bolster|prop up}}
#: {{ux|en|My family '''shored''' me up after I failed the [[GED]].}}
#: {{ux|en|The workers were '''shoring''' up the dock after part of it fell into the water.}}

===Etymology 5===
Originally ''common-shore''.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete|except|Scotland}} A [[sewer]].<ref>{{R:Webster 1913}}</ref>
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Pericles|4|6|passage=Emptie olde receptacles, or common-'''shores''' of filthe.}}
#* {{RQ:Addison Italy|passage=I need not mention the old common-'''shore''' of Rome.}}

===Etymology 6===
Uncertain. The word is attested in Northern English and Scots; the ''DSL'' states that ''schore'' "to threaten" is attested before 1400 (a corresponding noun ''schoyr'' is attested since 1375: "vith gret schoyr and mannasyng" in Barbour's ''Bruce''), and suggests it might ultimately be related to Old Scots ''schoir'' "steep (of a crag)", related to ''shear''. Alternatively, it has been suggested that it might be a variant of {{m|en|score}} or {{m|en|sure}} and related to {{m|en|assure}}. 

====Verb====
{{en-verb}} {{tlb|en|transitive|Scotland|archaic}}

# To [[threaten]] or [[warn]] unpleasant consequences (for someone); {{lb|en|sometimes}} to threaten or [[warn]] off or scare away.
#* <!--drive away or scare off?--> {{quote-book|en|year=1810|author=Robert-Hartley Cromek|title=Remains of Nithsdale and Galloway Song: with Historical and Traditional Notices Relative to the Manners and Customs of the Peasantry. Now First Published|page=98
|text=The Gleds might pyked her at the dyke, Before the lads wad '''shored''' them off her.}}
#* <!--threatened? assured?--> {{quote-book|en|year=1866|author=Allan Ramsay|title=The Poetical Works, with Selections from the Scottish Poets Before Burns|page=59
|text=Bess flew till him {{...}} and with her fatal Knife '''shored''' she would geld him, For peace that day.}}
#* <!--?--> {{quote-book|en|year=1891|author=James Logie Robertson|title=Ochil Idylls: And Other Poems|page=66
|text=... a' the freits that were begun To '''shore''' us ill Shall, in the crackin' of a gun, Flee owre the hill.}}
# {{lb|en|of weather, clouds, etc}} To [[threaten]] (to rain).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1733|author=Allan Ramsay|title=Poems: By Allan Ramsay. With New Additions and Notes|chapter=A Pastoral on the death of M. Prior|page=210
|text=For a' our tears and sighs are but in vain: Come, help me up; — yon sooty cloud '''shores''' rain.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1860|author=William Watt|title=Poems, on sacred and other subjects; and songs, humorous and sentimental ... Third edition of the songs only-with additional songs|page=34
|text={{...}} the cauld win' louder blew, '''Shorin{{'}}''' o' drift,{{nb...}}}}
# To [[offer]] or present (someone something).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1878|author=David Vedder|title=Poems, lyrics, and sketches|page=124
|text=... a compliment kindly and decently '''shored''', {{...}}}}
